domthron.name: Aachen Cathedral
domthron.slogan: Charlemagne's octagon, still holding up the sky after 1,200 years.
domthron.line: One of the first 12 sites on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1978, it was where 31 German kings were crowned between 936 and 1531.

kroenungssaal.name: Aachen Town Hall
kroenungssaal.slogan: A coronation feast hall built on an emperor's palace walls.
kroenungssaal.line: Built from 1330 to 1349 on the foundations of Charlemagne's palace hall, it still incorporates the Carolingian Granus Tower.

roteshausmonschau.name: Rotes Haus, Monschau
roteshausmonschau.slogan: The cloth barons' red mansion, and its show-stopping wooden staircase.
roteshausmonschau.line: The Scheibler cloth-making family's double house, finished in 1768, is now a museum of 18th and 19th century bourgeois living.

elisenbrunnen.name: Elisenbrunnen
elisenbrunnen.slogan: A neoclassical colonnade pouring hot, eggy spa water.
elisenbrunnen.line: Opened in 1827 to a design revised by Karl Friedrich Schinkel, it serves sulphur water at about 52 degrees Celsius.

burgnideggen.name: Burg Nideggen
burgnideggen.slogan: A Jülich fortress perched over the Rur valley.
burgnideggen.line: Count Wilhelm II of Jülich founded it in 1177, and its keep became North Rhine-Westphalia's first castle museum in 1979.
